If every meaningful change still waits for my approval, the project remains dependent on me. Its files may survive while its judgment disappears."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"When I say I want to build a legacy, I can make the sentence sound nobler than a wish for fame. The more useful question is practical: who can carry the work when I stop?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Quality gives people a reason to care. Survival requires adoption, reinterpretation, and a transfer of responsibility. That makes legacy a custody problem."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"What survives the creator"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Virality, fame, and legacy differ in what they preserve. A viral post preserves attention for a short time. Fame preserves recognition of a person. Legacy begins when value moves into something other people can use without requiring the creator's presence."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The most useful test is decoupling. Would the work still function if I stopped explaining it, repairing it, or speaking on its behalf? Popularity says little about survival through a funding cycle, a change of leadership, or a decade of neglect. A famous person can leave no durable structure, while an almost forgotten person can shape a practice used every day."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attention still matters. Work must enter other people's lives before they can decide to carry it."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attention gets work adopted"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A standard, tool, or idea becomes part of ordinary life after people notice it, test it, argue about it, and put it to use. Good design cannot place itself into the world."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The internet offers a useful example because adoption did not happen through a single act. "},{"type":"text","text":"RFC 801","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc801.txt"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" laid out ARPANET's transition from NCP to TCP/IP years in advance, including relay hosts that could speak both protocols. Implementers still had to convert individual hosts and services."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Later, OSI had an international standard, government backing, and an ambitious architecture. TCP/IP spread through working implementations, Berkeley Unix, and protocols that could be implemented without buying ISO documents. Andrew L. Russell describes that competition in "},{"type":"text","text":"“OSI: The Internet That Wasn't”","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://spectrum.ieee.org/osi-the-internet-that-wasnt"}}]},{"type":"text","text":". Design mattered, but distribution and use gave TCP/IP momentum."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reputation can help a useful artifact cross the gap between existence and use. A trusted name may persuade a stranger to read a specification or try a tool. Attention becomes corrosive when accumulating an audience becomes the purpose of the work."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Refusing all attention can become another form of vanity, especially when the work needs people before it can matter. I try to remember what the attention is for."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Custody keeps work alive"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I once described legacy as a permanent modification to baseline reality. I no longer think permanence is a serious target. It is a romantic word that hides how human structures actually survive."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Institutions get captured. Standards are superseded. Philosophies are read selectively under conditions their authors could not imagine. Even an old idea changes as each generation decides what to keep, discard, or bend toward a new purpose."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Durability across reinterpretation is a more honest target. Work survives because people can revise it without making it useless. It persists through argument, translation, partial loss, and changes in ownership."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"This is where custody enters. Custody means more than storage. A public repository can remain online while its purpose quietly dies. Someone must interpret the work, accept changes, reject bad ones, settle disputes, transfer authority, and teach new people why it exists."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Custody does not always require a formal institution. Ideas can be held by readers, teachers, users, and communities with no central authority. What matters is that interpretation, repair, and responsibility no longer depend on the author alone."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Python offers a more formal example. Guido van Rossum stepped down as BDFL in July 2018. "},{"type":"text","text":"PEP 13","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://peps.python.org/pep-0013/"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" established an elected steering council, the first council was seated in 2019, and releases continued under that governance. Authority moved into a process that could survive its founder's departure."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Governance also has to survive its current governors. A project held together by one benevolent maintainer has only deferred the problem. Real custody includes succession: a way for judgment and authority to move before absence turns into crisis."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"That leaves me with a stricter sentence:"}]},{"type":"blockquote","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Legacy is what other people can carry without you."}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Carrying implies effort and freedom. The next custodian must be able to repair the work and also change it. If every meaningful decision still requires the founder's blessing, custody has never really moved."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The authority I still hold"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"MCP Visor is a public, MIT-licensed, self-hosted proxy. It intercepts MCP "},{"type":"text","text":"tools/call","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" requests before relay and evaluates them against policy. Making the repository available is easy compared with transferring the judgment behind it."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The custody test changes the questions I ask about its future. Does anyone run it who has never spoken to me? The harder question is whether someone else has both the context and the commit rights to say no."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Writing more code would still leave me at the center. A durable project needs enough context for someone else to make decisions, including decisions I might have made differently. Authority has to move as well."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"That prospect exposes the emotional part of custody. I like being able to say that I built the thing. Shared authority weakens the clean line between the work and my identity, even as it gives the work a better chance of continuing."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I do not yet know how to make that transfer. For now, the question tells me what remains unfinished."}]}]}
draft.draft_subtitle: Would the work still function if you stopped?
